name: From Fire to Fusion
description: The story of energy from the first campfire to the dream of fusion: wood, water, steam, oil, electricity and the atom.

checkpoints.name: Muscle and flame
checkpoints.note: For most of human history energy meant muscle, wood and fat. Fire, then lamps and the first water wheels, gave people light, heat and work beyond their own strength.

checkpoints.name: Wind, water and steam
checkpoints.note: Windmills and watermills spread, and in the early eighteenth century steam engines begin to pump mines. James Watt makes them efficient, and steam power drives the Industrial Revolution.

checkpoints.name: Electricity arrives
checkpoints.note: Faraday's discoveries lead to motors, and batteries and lamps appear. Edison builds a power station in New York, Tesla's alternating current wins the War of the Currents, hydropower and wind turbines begin, and oil and diesel start a new age.

checkpoints.name: Oil and the atom
checkpoints.note: The jet engine and the first nuclear reactor show that new fuels can change the world, as oil becomes the main fuel for transport.

checkpoints.name: Atoms, sun and the fusion dream
checkpoints.note: OPEC, formed in 1960, gives oil producers a shared voice. Nuclear plants, solar cells and lithium batteries spread, accidents at Chernobyl and Fukushima show the risks, and scientists build giant machines to try to copy the Sun.
